newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Tuesday remained inactive, with no reported sales, feedlot sources said.
A few packer bids at $66.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00, sources said.
The bulk of last week's sales were at $67.00 although there were light sales early in the week $68.00.

Sales this week were expected at $68.00 amid outlooks for continued firm beef prices. Light support also was seen from a decline in this week's showlists from last week's numbers, several cattle feeders said.

Trade this week was not expected until Wednesday or Thursday because packers had enough live cattle inventories to supply slaughter needs this week, sources said. As a result, packer buyers probably will wait as long as possible before buying more cattle, they said.
Beef sales so far this week have been light to moderate. Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.04 to down $0.10 per cwt on 209 fabricated loads sold.
Fed cattle prices could be pressured if CME live cattle futures turn sharply lower, some sources said.

CME live cattle futures started the week higher, partly buoyed by three consecutive days of limit gains in neighboring pork complex pits linked to prospects for greater pork exports. The greater exports were seen coming on news that Taiwan, a key competitor of the U.S. for pork exports on the world market, had banned pork exports due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease in hogs there.
However, cattle futures slipped Tuesday morning in sympathy with a drop in hog futures and on gains in CBOT corn futures, traders noted.
